subject: Creativity
title: IQ and Creativity: Smarter Doesn't Mean More Creative
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: IQ and Creativity: Smarter Doesn't Mean More Creative.

hook.text: The highest IQ ever recorded belonged to William Sidis (250-300). His greatest achievement?

buildup.text: Lewis Terman tracked 1,500+ high-IQ children from the 1920s through their lives.

discovery.text: Research shows a 'threshold effect' — IQ above about 120 adds little to creative output.

twist.text: The two future Nobel laureates in Terman's study area were REJECTED from his high-IQ group — Shockley and Alvarez.

climax.text: Creativity requires divergent thinking, risk tolerance, domain expertise, and intrinsic motivation — none of which IQ.

punchline.text: Intelligence opens doors. Creativity decides which ones are worth walking.

quiz.question: What is the 'threshold effect' regarding IQ and creativity?
options: Higher IQ always means more creativity
Above about 120 IQ, additional intelligence adds little to creative output

details.summary: Above-average intelligence correlates with creativity only up to a point. Beyond an IQ of about 120, additional intelligence does not predict greater creativity. Creative achievement depends more on personality traits, motivation, and domain expertise than raw cognitive ability.
details.whyItMatters: Separating IQ from creativity liberates people of ordinary intelligence from believing they cannot be creative. The most important factors in creative success are effort and personality, not test scores.
takeaways: Above IQ 120, intelligence and creativity do not correlate
Openness to experience predicts creativity better than IQ
Domain expertise and motivation matter more than raw intelligence

faq.question: What is the threshold theory of creativity?
faq.answer: Threshold theory proposes that a minimum level of intelligence is needed for creative work, but above that threshold, additional IQ adds little. The threshold is roughly an IQ of 120. Beyond it, personality and motivation drive creative differences.

faq.question: Which personality traits predict creativity?
faq.answer: Openness to experience is the strongest personality predictor of creativity. High tolerance for ambiguity, intrinsic motivation, willingness to take risks, and persistence in the face of failure also distinguish highly creative individuals.
